40892.name: TJS-1
40892.significance: Qianshao-3 class with large deployable antenna at 155.0°E. Dedicated signals intelligence collection platform.

41911.name: TJS-2
41911.significance: Suspected Huoyan-1 class missile early warning satellite positioned at 107.5°E / 66.5°E.

43874.name: TJS-3
43874.significance: Deployed a sub-satellite; conducted manoeuvres assessed as TTPs to deceive space domain awareness trackers. Has approached US military communications satellites.

44637.name: TJS-4
44637.significance: Qianshao-3 class signals intelligence collection platform positioned at 83.5°E.

44978.name: TJS-5
44978.significance: Huoyan-1 class missile early warning satellite positioned at 178.5°E / 107.5°E.

47613.name: TJS-6
47613.significance: Huoyan-1 class missile early warning satellite positioned at 178.5°E.

50574.name: TJS-9
50574.significance: Qianshao-3 class signals intelligence collection platform positioned at 137.2°E.

58204.name: TJS-10
58204.significance: Sustained, synchronised proximity operations with TJS-3 for dual-satellite communications and inspection testing. Key RPO capability demonstration.

62374.name: TJS-12
62374.significance: Huoyan class missile early warning satellite at 146.5°E. CZ-3B launched Dec 2024.

62804.name: TJS-14
62804.significance: Huoyan class at 18.4°E. First PRC missile warning satellite at a Western longitude — extends coverage toward European theatre.

63157.name: TJS-15
63157.significance: CZ-3B launched Mar 2025 with ejected apogee kick motor. New subseries; mission profile under assessment. Positioned at 90.3°E / 94.4°E.

63397.name: TJS-16
63397.significance: CZ-7A launched Mar 2025. Possibly Huoyan-2 series. Positioned at 152.5°E / 160.6°E.

63524.name: TJS-17
63524.significance: CZ-3B launched Apr 2025 with ejected AKM. Same new subseries as TJS-15. Positioned at 152.8°E / 164.5°E.

63924.name: TJS-19
63924.significance: CZ-3C launched May 2025 with ejected AKM. Positioned at 141.2°E. Mission profile under assessment.

41838.name: SJ-17
41838.significance: Equipped with a robotic arm. Has conducted numerous close approaches to both foreign and domestic satellites. Primary Chinese GEO inspection and ASAT platform.

49330.name: SJ-21
49330.significance: Demonstrated capability to physically relocate a satellite to a super-graveyard orbit. Refuelled by SJ-25 in 2025, extending operational endurance indefinitely.
49330.source: SWF Global Counterspace Capabilities 2025 / COSMIC Nov 2025

55131.name: SJ-23
55131.significance: GEO drift surveillance satellite. Monitors other GEO objects during drift phases. Part of China’s space domain awareness network.

62485.name: SJ-25
62485.significance: Demonstrated on-orbit refuelling of SJ-21 with ~142 kg hydrazine in 2025. Critical enabler for sustained ASAT operations and GEO fleet longevity.

50321.name: SY-12 01
50321.significance: Conducted close approach to US SBIRS GEO 6. Demonstrated advanced defensive manoeuvres against a US GSSAP satellite. Active counter-SDA capability.

50322.name: SY-12 02
50322.significance: Paired inspector with SY-12 01. Conducted joint close approach to US SBIRS GEO 6. Demonstrated advanced defensive manoeuvres against GSSAP.

65486.name: SY-29
65486.significance: CZ-3C/YZ-1 launched Sep 2025 to inclined GEO (29°) at 95°E. Mission profile under assessment.

41194.name: Gaofen-4
41194.significance: Optical GEO surveillance satellite. Resolution sufficient to track large naval vessels. Foundational layer of China’s persistent GEO ISR architecture.

46610.name: Gaofen-13
46610.significance: 15m resolution GEO optical satellite. Persistent monitoring of fixed and mobile targets. Dual civil/military utility; supports PLA targeting.

55912.name: Gaofen-13-02
55912.significance: Successor to Gaofen-13 with similar 15m optical capability. Redundant persistent GEO surveillance; supports PLA kill chain.

58582.name: Yaogan-41
58582.significance: New large high-resolution GEO optical satellite. Provides persistent stare over the Indo-Pacific. Key enabler for PLA kill chains for anti-ship and land-attack missions.

57624.name: Ludi Tance-4 01A
57624.significance: World’s only GEO SAR satellite. Provides all-weather, 24/7 surveillance capability. Negates cloud cover as concealment for surface targets.

62188.name: TJS-13
62188.significance: CZ-3B launched Dec 2024 to Molniya orbit. Suspected Huoyan-1 class providing missile early warning coverage of high-latitude regions.

49258.name: Shiyan-10
49258.significance: Operating in an unusual Molniya orbit. Assessed as testing new concepts for high-latitude coverage. Precursor to TJS-13/21 HEO series.

65563.name: Yaogan-45
65563.significance: China’s first large EO satellite in MEO (~7,500 km, 20° inclination). Paradigm shift: persistent wide-area surveillance enhancing PLA targeting kill chains for anti-ship and land-attack operations.

40258.name: Luch / Olymp-K
40258.significance: Long history of close approaches to Western GEO satellites for suspected SIGINT collection. Capable intelligence platform, now less active than its successor Olymp-2.

55841.name: Luch / Olymp-2
55841.significance: Active GEO inspector. Continues pattern of close approaches (10–60 km) to Western military and commercial satellites for suspected SIGINT and intimidation. Targeted Wideband Global SATCOM and Eutelsat assets.

64467.name: Cosmos 2589
64467.significance: HEO parent bus operating in highly elliptical synchronous orbit. Deployed the manoeuvrable Cosmos 2590 sub-satellite. May have docked with 2590 in Sep 2025. Assessed as high-orbit Nivelir/Burevestnik ASAT variant.

64527.name: Cosmos 2590
64527.significance: Manoeuvrable HEO sub-satellite released from Cosmos 2589. Capable of close-approach operations at GEO altitudes. Assessed as potential co-orbital ASAT weapon (Nivelir programme). Separated Nov 2025.

65590.name: Cosmos 2595
65590.significance: GLONASS-K1 navigation satellite launched Sep 2025. New-generation digital GLONASS. Critical Russian military PNT infrastructure sustaining precision guidance despite sanctions.

53370.name: Khayyam
53370.significance: Iran’s most capable satellite. Russian-built Kanopus-V derivative with ~1m resolution. Direct military utility for targeting and surveillance. Operated from Shahroud under IRGC control.

58817.name: Sorayya
58817.significance: Launched on Qaem-100 to 750 km — highest orbit achieved by Iran. Technology demonstrator for solid-fuel IRGC space launch capability.

61072.name: Chamran-1
61072.significance: First Iranian satellite to demonstrate on-orbit manoeuvre capability. IRGC direct military asset. Establishes Iranian RPO/proximity operations precedent.

59065.name: Pars-1
59065.significance: 15m resolution remote sensing satellite. Launched on Russian Soyuz. Part of the ISA civil remote sensing programme with potential dual-use utility.

61769.name: Kowsar
61769.significance: Earth observation satellite with attitude control issues. Intermittent contact only. Limited operational utility in current state.

61768.name: Kowsar-1.5
61768.significance: IoT communications satellite. Reported intermittent operation (turning on and off) since Jun 2025. Degraded status.

64889.name: Nahid-2
64889.significance: First Iranian Ku-band telecommunications satellite. Simorgh-launched Dec 2025. Advances Iranian independent communications capability.

67264.name: Kowsar-2
67264.significance: Improved Kowsar variant. Soyuz-launched Dec 2025. Part of Iran’s expanding LEO earth observation constellation.

67255.name: Zafar-2
67255.significance: Soyuz-launched Dec 2025. Fregat upper stage anomaly noted by McDowell. Successor to Zafar-1 which failed to achieve orbit in 2020.

67280.name: Paya
67280.significance: Soyuz-launched Dec 2025. ISA acknowledged orbital injection challenges. Status uncertain pending confirmation of operational parameters.
